# Models

## LDA: Implementation & Tuning

**Purpose**

Observed shifts in approval ages and other numerical predictors provide a basis for comparing class means using a low-variance linear classifier.

**Pre-Processing**

Additionally removed linear dependencies among predictors and dropped predictors correlated above 0.9.

**Model**

Trained with `lda2` method to tune `dimen` --- the number of discriminant functions used.

Two class priors were trained and compared:

- Empirical: Follows training class proportions.

- Equal: Shift decision boundaries toward minority tiers to counter class imbalance. Selection Metric: Macro F1 with equal weight for classes.

## LDA: Results

| Model | Dimension | Macro F1 | Accuracy | Below NQS Recall | Meeting NQS Recall | Above NQS Recall |
|:----------|:----------|----------:|----------:|----------:|----------:|----------:|
| Empirical | 1 | 0.41 | 0.74 | 0.00 | 0.93 | 0.31 |
| Empirical | 2 | 0.43 | 0.74 | 0.03 | 0.92 | 0.32 |
| Equal     | 1 | 0.38 | 0.40 | 0.60 | 0.32 | 0.65 |
| Equal     | 2 | 0.44 | 0.51 | 0.53 | 0.48 | 0.60 |

The best performing model is the Equal LDA model with dimension of 2 at Marco F1 score of 0.44. The Empirical model with the same dimension scored 0.43. The 0.01 difference might be noise.

Equal prior LDA shows lower accuracy score due to penalizing predicting the majority class.
